name: Inkling
description: A calm place for your notes, to-dos and flashcards. It works offline and you never sign up for anything.

hero.lede: A calm place for your notes, to-dos and flashcards. It works offline and you never sign up for anything.
notes: If Windows says it protected your PC, click More info, then Run anyway.
hero.away: Inkling runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. Open this page on your computer to download it.

features.label: Today
features.title: Every to-do on one page
body: Every open checkbox, from every note, shows up on one page called Today. Tick it there and it is ticked in the note too.
The decks with cards due wait on the same page.

main.name: today
main.alt: The Today page with nine open to-dos from six notes and three decks with cards due

features.label: Flashcards
features.title: Flashcards from your notes
body: Write <kbd>Term :: Definition</kbd> in any note and that line becomes a flashcard. Each card comes back right before you would forget it.
Rate a card with the keys <kbd>1</kbd> to <kbd>4</kbd> and keep going.

main.name: study
main.alt: A flashcard for osmosis with its answer and the Again, Hard, Good and Easy buttons

features.label: Search
features.title: Find anything with <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>
body: <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> finds any note, to-do or deck, and <kbd>Ctrl+N</kbd> starts a new note. Your hands stay on the keyboard.

main.name: search
main.alt: The search window over Today with results for the word cell

pair.label: Themes
pair.title: A light and a dark theme
body: Pick one in Settings. The window opens in your theme from the very first frame.

assistant.label: AI assistant
assistant.title: Use Inkling with your AI assistant
body: Open Settings in Inkling and click Connect next to your assistant, then restart it. It can now search your notes, tidy them up, plan your day with you and quiz you on the flashcards that are due.
Another assistant? Click Copy setup in the same place and paste it into its MCP settings. Inkling fills in where it is installed.

Nothing is deleted for good: a deleted note waits in the trash for 30 days, the assistant can undo its edits, and your data is backed up before its first change. The assistant starts Inkling itself and nothing goes over the network.
Want your assistant to know Inkling inside out? Download the skill.
assistant.caption: Copy setup gives you this, with your own path

items: Connect an AI assistant from Settings in one click. It can edit sections and text, rename notes, use the trash, see Today, quiz you on due flashcards and undo its own edits.
Your data is backed up before an assistant's first change in a session, and open notes show its changes within seconds.
New note sits at the top of the sidebar; Shortcuts and Settings moved to its foot.
<kbd>F1</kbd> shows every keyboard shortcut. <kbd>Ctrl+1</kbd> opens Today, <kbd>Ctrl+2</kbd> opens Flashcards.
Search lists Today, Flashcards, Settings and the shortcuts too, so you can jump there by name.
A new note starts with the cursor in its title, and one you leave completely empty is removed when you move on.
Delete is now in the note's toolbar.
Clicking a to-do's text on Today ticks it.
Adding a card: <kbd>Enter</kbd> moves from the question to the answer, then adds the card. Review buttons show their keys.
Long titles wrap onto a second line, and big titles no longer cut off the bottom of letters like g and y.

requirements: macOS on Intel or Apple Silicon
About 120 MB to download on Windows
No account and no internet connection

privacy.title: Nothing leaves your computer
body: Inkling has no account and no analytics. It goes online for one thing: at start, it checks for a new version.

data.title: One file you own
body: Your notes, to-dos and cards live in one file, inkling.db, in your user folder. Each start puts a backup next to it, and the last five are kept.
The export button above a note saves it as Markdown.

keys: Search, or jump to Today, Flashcards and Settings
Show the answer in a review

basics.title: Get started
steps: Open it. Inkling installs itself and opens.

basics.title: Updates
body: On Windows and Linux, Inkling downloads new versions by itself and installs them when you close it. On a Mac, download the new version from this page.

basics.title: Removing it
body: On Windows, uninstall it under Settings, Apps, Installed apps. Your notes stay in %APPDATA%\Inkling until you delete that folder.

a: Yes. There is no account, no subscription and nothing to unlock.

faq.q: Why does Windows say it protected my PC?
a: Inkling is not signed with a paid certificate, so Windows warns about it the first time. Click More info, then Run anyway.
In one file, inkling.db: in %APPDATA%\Inkling on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/Inkling on macOS and ~/.config/Inkling on Linux. The last five backups sit next to it.
Yes, all of it. Inkling only goes online at start, to look for a new version.

faq.q: Which AI assistants work with Inkling?
a: Any app that takes MCP servers. Settings connects the assistant apps it finds on your computer in one click; for any other, Copy setup gives you what to paste.

faq.q: Can I take my notes with me?
a: Yes. The export button above a note saves it as Markdown, and everything else is one SQLite file you can copy.

faq.q: How do the flashcards know when to come back?
a: Each time you rate a card, Inkling works out when you are about to forget it and schedules it for then. Cards you know well come back less often.
